sus.reason: I would like to make books for Lily, but this one was not good enough for me to want to use the website often.
The form was long and the technical wording made it feel more complicated than it needed to be.
The main buttons were easy to find, but the confusing messages and storybook controls made it awkward overall.
I managed without help, but I would probably have needed my grandson to explain some of the strange errors and settings.
The steps generally followed on from one another, but the book did not keep the important details from my story.
The spelling mistakes, wrong illustration style, technical errors, and incomplete ending did not fit together properly.
Most people familiar with ordinary websites might get started, but this would be difficult for anyone with poor eyesight or little technical confidence.
The long form, tiny page arrows, scrolling at 200% zoom, and need to check everything carefully made it cumbersome.
I felt reasonably confident filling in the form, but I did not feel confident that the finished book was correct.
I had to learn what terms like Lexile meant and work out what the errors and checkout choices meant.

interview.purpose: This website is for making personalised storybooks with family members and special memories. It seems intended for parents, grandparents, and other people wanting a keepsake for a child.
interview.worst_moment: The most frustrating moment was seeing the finished book. It had the wrong title spelling, did not use the Watercolour style I chose, left Conker out of the pictures, and ended with an unfinished sentence. It felt like the workshop had made the wrong box entirely.
interview.best_moment: The best moment was choosing the watercolour illustrations and pressing the large button to create the book. That part was clear and the orange button was easy to hit.
interview.abandon: I would not have given up while filling in the form, because the questions were mostly understandable. I would have stopped before paying because the book was not suitable, and I would have been worried about the gift wrap being ticked for me.
interview.missing: I expected to see Conker, Lily, Harold, the shed, Christmas, and the imaginary gallop across the Norfolk fields. I also expected a clear, large way to read every page and fix the story before ordering.
interview.trust: I was cautious about trusting it with family information. I entered the details because I was testing it, but the technical error, wrong pictures, unfinished ending, and pre-ticked gift wrap made me doubt whether it was handling my story properly.
interview.willingty_to_pay: I would not pay for this version. I would consider paying around £25 for a good hardcover if the story, pictures, and proof were right. I would pay more only if I could edit the book myself and be certain there were no extra charges.
interview.output_verdict: I was disappointed. The site remembered a few names, but it lost the heart of the story and produced something I would not give to Lily.

recommendations.change: Make the book follow the real memory: Harold carving Conker, giving it to Lily at Christmas, and Lily riding it across the Norfolk fields.
recommendations.why: Those details are the whole reason I wanted to make the book.

recommendations.change: Fix all spelling, grammar, repeated sentences, unfinished sentences, and unresolved name placeholders.
recommendations.why: A book with obvious mistakes is not fit to give to a child or keep as a family memory.

recommendations.change: Use the selected Watercolour style and show Conker, Lily, Harold, the workshop, and the fields accurately in the pictures.
recommendations.why: The pictures should match the words and the style I chose, especially for a present.

recommendations.change: Use simple, warm language suitable for a four-year-old instead of words such as “ephemeral luminescence” and frightening toothed shadows.
recommendations.why: Lily is only four, and I want the story to be comforting and easy for her to hear.

recommendations.change: Make the preview a clear page-reading area with large, labelled Previous and Next buttons.
recommendations.why: The little arrow buttons were difficult to use at 200% zoom, and I need to inspect every page myself.

recommendations.change: Explain clearly when information is saved, and say what Back and Next will do without losing later answers.
recommendations.why: I need to know my words are safe before carrying on.

recommendations.change: Show the 200-character limit before I reach it and tell me when text has been shortened.
recommendations.why: I do not want the important parts of my memory to disappear without warning.

recommendations.change: Replace pale text with darker, larger text and make footer and legal text readable.
recommendations.why: Pale grey writing is almost invisible to me, and I must be able to read every instruction and detail.

recommendations.change: Remove the unexplained technical error and replace it with a plain explanation of what happened and what I should do.
recommendations.why: An error after login made me wonder whether I had done something wrong.

recommendations.change: Explain reading levels in ordinary language and suggest the right level for a four-year-old.
recommendations.why: “Lexile” is a workshop label I do not understand, and the chosen level was far too advanced.

recommendations.change: Do not tick gift wrap automatically, and show every charge in one clear summary before payment.
recommendations.why: I do not want an extra £7.99 selected without my asking.

recommendations.change: Remove the count-down pressure and provide a clear way to leave checkout without losing my place.
recommendations.why: I need time to read the costs and terms without being hurried.

one_line_verdict: The workshop door was easy to find, but the book came out like the wrong piece of furniture, so I would not use it for Lily.
